newsitem.title: USA: US MMS royalties proposal better, needs work-IPAA.
newsitem.headline: US MMS royalties proposal better, needs work-IPAA.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service has improved its plan to change the way federal oil royalties are assessed, but the plan still needs work, the Independent Petroleum Association of America said Thursday.

"We've come a long way, but certainly there's still some work," IPAA spokeswoman Kate Hutcheons said. "It's pretty clear MMS heard the industry ... and put out a revision that addresses industry's concerns," she said.
The MMS Wednesday released a proposal to give independent oil producers more chances to base royalties on gross sales proceeds instead of NYMEX futures prices or Alaska North Slope prices.
The IPAA has said it was concerned that the index prices in many cases would overstate prices received at the wellhead and would inflate royalties.
"It looks like MMS is looking back to the lease, rather than exclusively at NYMEX and the futures market. That's encouraging," Hutcheons said.
"We need to work with MMS and build up their confidence that it is fair market value at the lease. There is still work to be done in that area," she said.
Hutcheons said the IPAA was worried that the MMS proposal expressed concern that the gross proceeds valuation in some cases could undervalue royalties.

She said an industry task force will study details of the MMS plan to revamp its system of assessing royalties for oil extracted under federal leases, which have been based on oil companies' posted prices.

The MMS is trying to switch to a system of basing the royalties on futures or ANS prices unless sales were from "arm's length" transactions between unaffiliated parties with competing interests to reflect market value.
